evidence.quote: The Stripe API authenticates requests using HTTP Basic Auth. Provide your API key as the basic auth username value.
If you need to authenticate using bearer auth (for example, for a cross-origin request), use `-H "Authorization: Bearer
Stripe’s MCP server uses OAuth to authorise clients according to the MCP specification
The OAuth Connect flow allows you to customize the user’s experience by passing additional parameters to Stripe.
The Stripe API uses API keys to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in the Stripe Dashboard.
Test mode secret keys start with sk_test_ and have unrestricted access to their sandboxes.
The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API
A sample test API key is included in all the examples here, so you can test any example right away.

result.notes: Sign-up is fully self-serve: creating a Stripe account instantly grants sandbox/test-mode API keys (sk_test_) with no approval step. Auth is API-key-based, presented either as an HTTP Basic Auth username or as a Bearer token; OAuth2 exists both for Connect (platform-to-connected-account authorization) and for authorizing MCP clients (mcp.stripe.com), though it is not the primary way to call the core REST API. Official vendor-published MCP server (mcp.stripe.com) wraps most of the REST API via generic read/write tools plus dedicated tools. REST API is large (446 endpoints per apis.guru spec). Restricted API keys (rk_live_) can scope down permissions but require no special approval beyond a live account (which needs standard business verification for live mode, not developer API access).
result.one_liner: Stripe is a payments/fintech platform (payments, billing, connect, treasury) with a large REST API for building financial and commerce integrations.
